newsitem.title: JORDAN: Paris bourse to help automate Jordan market.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse to help automate Jordan market.

text.p: Jordan signed on Tuesday a deal with the Paris bourse to povide it with technical assistance to automate trading on the Amman stock exchange, stock market officials said.
Umayya Toukan, director of the Amman Financial Market (AMF), said the new system, to be financed by French government grants, could be up and running within 14 months.
It would settle deals instantly, replacing a laborious trading and clearing system which currently takes three days to settle transactions.
"It is a big leap that will help the stock exchange to attract domestic, Arab and foreign investment," said Toukan.

The contract, which defines the cooperation between SPF-Paris Bourse and SICOVAM SA (the French securities depository) and the AMF, is in three phases. Work on the project is to begin next month with a target of full automation by the end of the 14 months period.

Toukan said the new settlement system was part of a wider package of reforms aimed at making the market, on a downward trend for two years after a 1992-93 bull run, more transparent, efficient and investor-friendly.

A draft law is due to be put before Jordan's parliament soon which would tighten up regulations on accountability and transparency both for brokers and listed companies on the Amman Financial Market (AFM).
It will also toughen up rules against insider dealing, and separate the regulatory role of the AFM from its day-to-day trading supervision.

The Amman exchange, one of the most politically sensitive bourses in the region, was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
Already suffering from high domestic interest rates, market capitalisation fell nine percent to 2.9 billion dinars at the end of July from 3.2 billion at the start of the year.
Toukan, who has run the exchange since 1991, will leave his post and hand over on October 15 to Wahib Shair, senior national partner at Allied Accountants, a member firm of Arthur Andersen and Co.
